reason: The dividing basal cells and their nutrient supply suggest a way to renew the skin.
expectation: The cells will use the nutrients to produce replacement skin cells.

effect: The basal cells produced new skin cells, suggesting they can contribute to renewing the body’s skin.
reaction: The upward movement of older cells makes the renewal process clearer.
reason: The new cells appear ready to replace skin cells in the repaired body.
expectation: The body’s skin will be renewed with the new cells.

effect: The body is now renewing its skin; blood and bone renewal remain.
reaction: The link between new cells below and shedding at the surface is clear.
reason: Erythropoietin is shown as a kidney signal carried to marrow, where the red-cell precursors are located.
expectation: The signal will stimulate the precursors to produce red blood cells.

effect: The kidney signal has led the marrow precursors toward red-cell maturation; the developing cells may now be ready to join the body.
reaction: The low-oxygen cue makes the reason for the kidney signal clearer.
reason: The developing red cells appear to be the next part of blood renewal in the same body.
expectation: The body will gain a renewing supply of red blood cells.

effect: The body now renews skin and blood; bone renewal remains.
reaction: The link between the kidney signal and red-cell replacement is clear.
reason: The bone-removing and bone-forming cells appear to perform successive parts of bone renewal.
expectation: The cells will remove old bone matrix and replace it with new matrix.

effect: The bone-removing cells act on the body first; bone-forming cells likely follow to replace the removed matrix.
reaction: I expected the two cell types to combine directly, so the sequential action was a small surprise.
reason: The forming cells are shown depositing new matrix in the hollow left by removal.
expectation: The cells will deposit new bone matrix where old bone was removed.

effect: Bone-forming cells completed the renewal sequence, and the goal to renew skin, blood and bone is complete.
reaction: The final result makes the two stages of bone renewal clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making developing red cells was most worthwhile: the picture linked a low-oxygen cue at the kidney to a signal reaching marrow and cells maturing.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the new skin cells to the body was predictable after making them, although it showed where replacement and shedding happen.

surprise.text: I expected the bone-removing and bone-forming cells to combine directly. Instead, removal acted on the body first, followed by rebuilding.

arbitrary.text: The separate action to add developing red cells to the body felt somewhat mechanical, though the result showed them entering a vessel from marrow.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it offered more connections like the kidney signal and bone renewal. Several assembly steps were predictable, but the results helped explain how the tissues keep working.
